title: Genetic Factors Related to Severe COVID-19: Analysis of GWAS Data
author: Zhang, Lin, et al.
materials: COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative GWAS B1
COVID-19 Host Genetics Initiative GWAS B2

steps.title: Register for SAS OnDemand
steps.instruction: Create a free SAS OnDemand for Academics account at https://www.sas.com/en_us/software/on-demand-for-academics.html and log in to SAS Studio.

steps.title: Download COVID‑19 GWAS Analyzer
steps.instruction: From the GitHub repository https://github.com/chengzhongshan/COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer download the file COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer.zip to your local computer.

steps.title: Create Macros folder in SAS Studio
steps.instruction: In SAS Studio’s HOME directory (Files (HOME)) create a new folder named “Macros”.

steps.title: Upload macro files
steps.instruction: Extract COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer.zip locally and upload all SAS macro files contained in the extracted “Macros” sub‑directory to the SAS Studio “Macros” folder you just created.

steps.title: Load all SAS macros

substeps.instruction: Press F3 (or click the Submit button) to run the code. This step takes roughly 2 minutes and loads > 400 macros.
Optional: run %get_anno4macro to list macro annotations, or use %macroparas with a macro name to view its source.

steps.title: Download single‑cell dataset files
steps.instruction:
From the UCSC Cell Browser download the three files for the COVID‑19 hypertension dataset:
• https://cells.ucsc.edu/covid-hypertension/Seurat_umap.coords.tsv.gz
• https://cells.ucsc.edu/covid-hypertension/meta.tsv
• https://cells.ucsc.edu/covid-hypertension/exprMatrix.tsv.gz

steps.title: Upload single‑cell files to SAS
steps.instruction: Upload the three downloaded files (Seurat_umap.coords.tsv.gz, meta.tsv, exprMatrix.tsv.gz) into the HOME directory of SAS OnDemand for Academics.

steps.title: Import single‑cell data
steps.instruction:
Run the macro %import_sc_mtex_meta_umap_data with the following arguments (timing ≈ 30 min):
%import_sc_mtex_meta_umap_data(
  umap_file=%sysfunc(pathname(HOME))/Seurat_umap.coords.tsv.gz,
  meta_file=%sysfunc(pathname(HOME))/meta.tsv,
  cell_id_in_meta=cell,
  exp_matrix_file=%sysfunc(pathname(HOME))/exprMatrix.tsv.gz,
  outdir=%sysfunc(pathname(HOME)),
  target_genes=,
  mean_exp_cutoff=0.01,
  max_cells2import=1000000
);

substeps.instruction: The macro creates three SAS datasets in the HOME directory: exp (expression matrix with gene symbols), umap (UMAP coordinates merged with metadata), and headers (cell barcodes).
If the input matrix contains > 1 000 000 cells, the macro randomly selects 1 000 000 cells to stay within the ~5 GB disk quota of SAS OnDemand.

steps.title: Assign library reference
steps.instruction:
Define a libname that points to the HOME directory:
libname sc "%sysfunc(pathname(HOME))";

steps.title: Create UMAP plot
steps.instruction:
Generate a single‑cell UMAP using the imported dataset:
%sc_umap(umap_ds=sc.umap, xvar=x, yvar=y, cluster_var=cluster);

steps.title: Recode severity categories
Plot MAP3K19 expression
steps.instruction:
Create a UMAP visualization for gene MAP3K19, highlighting ciliated cells:
%sc_scatter4gene(
  dsd=sc.exp,
  dsd_headers=sc.headers,
  dsd_umap=sc.umap,
  gene=MAP3K19,
  pheno_var=severity,
  pheno_categories=Healthy Severe Critical,
  boxplot_width=800,
  boxplot_height=300,
  umap_width=400,
  umap_height=800,
  umap_lattice_nrows=3,
  boxplot_nrows=1,
  where_cnd4sgplot=%quote(cluster contains %'Ciliated%')
);

substeps.instruction: The macro internally creates a dataset named new__tgt_dsd_ that contains the cells used for the plot.

steps.title: Zoom into UMAP region
steps.instruction:
Restrict the UMAP axes to a specific X‑ and Y‑range:
%umap_with_axes_restriction(
  dsdin=new__tgt_dsd_,
  umap_width=1000,
  umap_height=300,
  lattice_or_not=0,
  raxis_max=20000,
  raxis_min=0,
  caxis_max=,
  caxis_min=45000,
  panel_row_num=1,
  noheader=0
);

steps.title: Prepare data for differential analysis
Generate frequency boxplots and run GLM
steps.instruction:
Run the macro %sc_freq_boxplot to compute cell‑type frequencies, plot boxplots, and perform differential expression with covariates:
%sc_freq_boxplot(
  longformdsd=tgt,
  cell_type_var=cell_type,
  sample_grp_var=sample,
  pheno_var=severity,
  cust_pheno_order=Healthy Severe Critical,
  exp_var=exp,
  exp_cutoff=-1,
  boxplot_height=800,
  boxplot_width=300,
  boxplot_nrows=5,
  where_cnd_for_sgplot=%quote(cell_type contains 'Ciliated' or cell_type='Other'),
  frqout=cellfrqout,
  other_glm_classes=sex medication Old CAD CVD hypertension,
  aggre_sc_glm_pdiff_dsd=all_sc
);

substeps.instruction: The macro calculates percentages (percent = cells/total_cells_in_a_pheno_grp) for each phenotype group.
Differential expression is performed on log10(reads+1).

steps.title: View differential expression results
steps.instruction:
Display the table of differential results generated by the previous step:
proc print data=all_sc_celltype_pdiff; run;

steps.title: Differential Z‑test between GWASs
steps.instruction:
For two GWAS summary files (e.g., HGI‑B1 and HGI‑B2) compute a differential Z‑score for each SNP with MAF > 0.01 and imputation score > 0.6 using the formula:
ΔZ‑score = (gwas1.β − gwas2.β) / sqrt(gwas1.se^2 + gwas2.se^2)
Then set diff.zscore = ΔZ‑score and calculate two‑sided p‑value:
P = 2 * pnorm(‑|diff.zscore|).
If normalization is desired, first standardize ΔZ‑score with PROC STDIZE (method=std) and then apply the same p‑value formula to the normalized Z‑scores.
All calculations can be scripted in SAS using DATA steps and PROC STDIZE as described in the protocol.

description: The protocol below describes the specific steps for using COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer to conduct integrative analyses of COVID-19 hospitalization GWASs from the Host Genetics Initiative (HGI).2 However, we have also used this protocol for analyzing GWASs from COVID-19 GRASP database,3 UK Biobank (UKB),4 and even users’ supplied GWAS data, such as long COVID GWAS data.5,6 To access the necessary tools, register for a free SAS OnDemand for Academics account by visiting this link (https://www.sas.com/en_us/software/on-demand-for-academics.html). SAS OnDemand for Academics provides cloud-based access to SAS Studio free of charge. The current protocol is tailored for execution in the SAS studio. Once you have obtained a SAS OnDemand for Academics account, download the COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer package in compressed zip format from its corresponding GitHub repository (https://github.com/chengzhongshan/COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer). In SAS Studio, create a directory called ‘Macros’ under the home directory ‘Files (HOME)’. Extract the downloaded file ‘COVID19_GWAS_Analyzer.zip’ on your local computer and upload all SAS macro files within the ‘Macros’ directory to the corresponding online SAS studio directory ‘Macros’.
